Eliphaz
EL-ih-faz
proper noun / person
From Hebrew ʾĒlīpāz; the Temanite, foremost of Job’s three friends, appealing to night visions and moral order (Job 2:11; 4–5; 15; 22).

Biblical Definition

Eliphaz the Temanite is the first of Job’s friends to speak, claiming a stealthy night word and arguing that trouble does not spring from the dust without cause (Job 4–5). He later hardens into direct accusation: is not thy wickedness great? He is the most solemn of the three and the one the LORD addresses when wrath is kindled against the friends (Job 42:7). Eliphaz therefore stands for elevated spiritual tone enlisted in a false charge. He can speak of God’s chastening and of seeking God, yet he cannot leave room for a blameless sufferer under heaven’s strange permission. Modern spirituality loves Eliphaz’s vibe: visions, maxims, and a neat moral universe. Scripture loves truth more than vibe. Hold Eliphaz, and fear impressive counsel that cannot survive the LORD’s own verdict. The friends must offer sacrifice and seek Job’s prayer; status as counselor is not innocence. The name stands in Scripture so that the church will not invent a thinner story than the one God wrote under providence. Webster 1828 Definition

Temanite friend of Job; first speaker; visionary tone; rebuked by the LORD with the others.

expand to see more

ELIPHAZ, the Temanite, friend of Job.

He spoke first among the three counselors.

He appealed to a night vision and moral order.

He later accused Job of great wickedness.

The LORD kindled wrath against him and his two friends.

Key Scripture

Job 2:11 — "Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him."

Job 4:1 — "Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,"

Job 22:5 — "Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?"

Job 42:7 — "And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath."

Modern Corruption

Eliphaz is treated as a wisdom brand; Job shows elevated counsel can still be false before God.

expand to see more

The corruption is to baptize tone as truth. Eliphaz sounds deep and still errs. Recover the LORD’s verdict over spiritual aesthetics.

A second misuse is to weaponize chastening doctrine against every sufferer. Recover fear in application.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Eliphaz is Job’s Temanite friend whose solemn counsel ends under divine rebuke.

Usage

"Eliphaz the Temanite answered Job."

"The LORD spoke to Eliphaz concerning the friends’ error."

"Eliphaz accused Job with solemn wrongness."
